hints: At the greatest height, the vertical velocity of the particle is instantaneously zero ($v = 0$).
Use the constant acceleration equation $v = u + at$ with initial speed $u = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and acceleration $a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Solve the equation $0 = 25 - 10t$ for the time $t$.
walkthrough:
Apply the kinematic formula $v = u + at$ with $u = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at greatest height, and $a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$0 = 25 - 10t$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the physical condition for maximum height during vertical motion under gravity: the vertical speed becomes instantaneously zero:
$$v = 0\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The motion is subject to constant gravitational deceleration:
$$a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
The initial upward velocity is:
$$u = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

State the constant acceleration formula connecting velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and time:
$$v = u + at$$
Substitute the known values:
$$0 = 25 + (-10)t$$
$$0 = 25 - 10t$$

Add $10t$ to both sides of the equation:
$$10t = 25$$
Divide by $10$:
$$t = \frac{25}{10} = 2.5\text{ s}$$
Thus the time taken to reach the greatest height is $2.5\text{ s}$.

hints: Since the particle is projected from $3\text{ m}$ above the ground, a height of $23\text{ m}$ corresponds to a displacement of $s = 23 - 3 = 20\text{ m}$ from the projection point.
Set up the displacement-time equation $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $s = 20\text{ m}$, $u = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and $a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Solve the resulting quadratic equation for the two times when the particle is at height $23\text{ m}$.
Subtract the earlier time from the later time to find the duration for which the particle is above $23\text{ m}$.
walkthrough:
Determine the displacement from the projection point when the particle is $23\text{ m}$ above the ground:
$$s = 23 - 3 = 20\text{ m}$$

Set up the constant acceleration equation $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $u = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$20 = 25t - \frac{1}{2}(10)t^2$$
$$5t^2 - 25t + 20 = 0$$

Solve the quadratic equation by dividing through by $5$:
$$t^2 - 5t + 4 = 0$$
$$(t - 1)(t - 4) = 0$$
$$t = 1\text{ s} \quad \text{and} \quad t = 4\text{ s}$$

Calculate the length of time the particle is higher than $23\text{ m}$:
$$\Delta t = 4 - 1 = 3\text{ s}$$

ai_rubric.Modelling Vertical Motion: Forms $20 = 25t - 5t^2$ to find crossing times and computes time duration $4 - 1 = 3\text{ s}$.
ai_rubric.Solving Quadratic Equations: Solves $t^2 - 5t + 4 = 0$ to get roots $t = 1\text{ s}$ and $t = 4\text{ s}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
Note the starting position: particle $P$ is launched from an initial height of $3\text{ m}$ above ground. Therefore, when $P$ is at a height of $23\text{ m}$ above the ground, its vertical displacement $s$ from the point of projection is:
$$s = 23 - 3 = 20\text{ m}$$

State the constant acceleration displacement formula:
$$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$$
Substitute $s = 20\text{ m}$, $u = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and $a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$20 = 25t + \frac{1}{2}(-10)t^2$$
$$20 = 25t - 5t^2$$

Rearrange into standard quadratic form:
$$5t^2 - 25t + 20 = 0$$
Divide every term by $5$:
$$t^2 - 5t + 4 = 0$$
Factor the quadratic:
$$(t - 1)(t - 4) = 0$$
Setting each factor to zero gives the two times $P$ passes through height $23\text{ m}$:
$$t_1 = 1\text{ s} \quad \text{(on the upward journey)}$$
$$t_2 = 4\text{ s} \quad \text{(on the downward journey)}$$

Find the duration during which the particle remains higher than $23\text{ m}$:
$$\text{Duration} = t_2 - t_1 = 4 - 1 = 3\text{ s}$$
Thus the particle is higher than $23\text{ m}$ for $3\text{ s}$.

hints: Because the vertical trajectory is symmetrical about the greatest height at $t = 2.5\text{ s}$, a time window of $1\text{ s}$ above height $h$ extends $0.5\text{ s}$ on either side of $t = 2.5\text{ s}$.
Identify the time when the particle first reaches height $h$: $t = 2.5 - 0.5 = 2\text{ s}$.
Calculate the vertical displacement $s$ from the projection point at $t = 2\text{ s}$ using $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$.
Add the initial height of $3\text{ m}$ to the displacement to find the total height $h$ above the ground.
walkthrough:
Use symmetry about the time of maximum height ($t = 2.5\text{ s}$) to find the time when the particle reaches height $h$:
$$t = 2.5 - 0.5 = 2.0\text{ s}$$

Calculate the vertical displacement from the projection point at $t = 2.0\text{ s}$ using $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$:
$$s = 25(2) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(2^2) = 50 - 20 = 30\text{ m}$$

Add the initial $3\text{ m}$ height above the ground to obtain $h$:
$$h = 3 + s = 3 + 30 = 33\text{ m}$$

ai_rubric.Modelling Vertical Motion: Uses symmetry to identify $t = 2\text{ s}$ and calculates $h = 3 + 25(2) - 5(2^2) = 33\text{ m}$.

teacher_walkthrough: Recall that vertical motion under gravity is symmetric about the apex. From part (i), the particle reaches its greatest height at $t = 2.5\text{ s}$.

The particle is above height $h$ for a total time interval of $1\text{ s}$. By symmetry, this interval must extend $0.5\text{ s}$ before and $0.5\text{ s}$ after the apex:
$$t_1 = 2.5 - 0.5 = 2.0\text{ s}$$
$$t_2 = 2.5 + 0.5 = 3.0\text{ s}$$
Thus the particle reaches height $h$ on the way up at $t = 2.0\text{ s}$.

Calculate the vertical displacement from the launch position at $t = 2.0\text{ s}$ using $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$:
$$s = 25(2) + \frac{1}{2}(-10)(2^2)$$
$$s = 50 - 5(4) = 50 - 20 = 30\text{ m}$$

Since the particle was projected from $3\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground, the height $h$ above ground is:
$$h = 3 + s = 3 + 30 = 33\text{ m}$$
Thus the value of $h$ is $33\text{ m}$.
